pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Closes #93. Upkeep’s first release preview rejected commit `398cdc2` because GitHub linked it to PR #4 on an intermediate branch.

```text
Upkeep #4 → feat/python-discovery
Upkeep #5 → main
  Complete PR #5 commit list matches the Git merge footprint
  Initial adoption records the introduced commit once under PR #5
```

The fallback requires the entire merge footprint to be within the configured onboarding range. Upkeep’s initial-commit baseline and PR #6 cutoff stay fixed.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: users
summary: "Recognize stacked pull requests during initial release adoption."
impact: "Historical changes linked to an intermediate branch are counted once at the release-branch merge when its commit list matches the Git footprint."
required_action: null
```

## Evidence

- **Before** — The Upkeep regression fixture failed when the introduced commit lacked a qualifying direct association with PR #5.
- **After** — The fixture counts the introduced commit once under PR #5. Negative fixtures reject an incomplete outer commit list, overlapping release-branch footprints, and missing direct attribution across the cutoff or without onboarding.

## Merge Danger

**Door** — Two-way.

**Blast radius** — Initial-adoption collection for corroborated merge footprints.

## Verification

- `pnpm verify` passed formatting, lint, type checks, all 818 tests, and the documentation build.
- Upkeep’s GitHub metadata was checked read-only. The fixture uses local Git history and mocked API responses.

## Summary

```diff
- Node.js 26.13.0
+ Node.js 26.13.1
```

Update the development and CI runtime pin and the packaged Alpine image. The image uses the official Docker Hub manifest-list digest for `node:26.13.1-alpine3.24`. [Node.js security release](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v26.13.1/)

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: users
summary: "Update the release-log container to Node.js 26.13.1."
impact: "The container includes fixes for seven High-severity Node.js vulnerabilities flagged by the image scan."
required_action: null
```

## Verification

- **Before** — Grype flagged seven High findings in the Node.js 26.13.0 binary in [PR #94's container-security run](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44617448375).
- **After** — Built the packaged image with `pnpm container:build`. With container networking disabled, `node --version` returned `v26.13.1` and the packaged CLI displayed help.
- The local container security gate passed with five Medium findings and zero High, Critical, or Unknown findings. Grype 0.121.2 used database v6.1.10, built 2026-11-19 18:41 UTC.
- The commit hook ran the same `pnpm check` suite as `pnpm verify` and passed all 814 tests and the documentation build. A concurrent standalone run timed out in the packed CLI test.

## Risks and limitations

This is a reversible runtime patch scoped to development, CI, and the packaged container. The CLI retains its existing Node.js compatibility range.

## Summary

Refs #78. The [proposed release-candidate spec](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/blob/5a536b0f9f58b72c38c8324e05e0389067113403/docs/spec/78-release-candidates.md) is pending owner approval.

```text
stable tag → rc.1 landing → rc.2 landing → stable promotion landing
     └──────── cumulative stable membership ────────────┘
```

The proposal covers activation, version numbering, candidate notes, cumulative stable notes, promotion, abandonment, and exact-landing tag recovery. It changes documentation only.

## Evidence

- The existing policy defines a stable-only stream. The proposal adds worked examples for candidate refresh, promotion, breaking feedback, abandonment, and conflicting or delayed tag writes.
- The normal commit hook ran `pnpm check` (the command behind `pnpm verify`) on Node 26.13.1. All 814 tests and the documentation build passed.

## Merge Danger

**Door** Two-way

**Blast radius** Documentation

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: Document a proposed release candidate and stable promotion policy.
impact: Maintainers can review worked version, membership, and recovery examples before implementation.
required_action: null
```

pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Propose the v1 local JSON contract for #77. For review:

- Bind each release to exact reviewed evidence and preserve its ID through proposed, tagged and published states.
- Use recorded tag and GitHub publication timestamps, with null for unavailable values.
- Require explicit audience selection. Fail public export if filtering would hide breaking information or a required action.

The implementation PR depends on agreement on these rules and on selecting concrete local review and publication evidence. Reviewed notes remain with #76. Reader-facing formats remain follow-up work under #77.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: "Propose a versioned JSON export contract for reviewed releases."
impact: "Maintainers can review the evidence, identity, timestamp and audience rules before implementation."
required_action: null
```

## Evidence

- Previously, #77 described the export goals and left the schema and audience rules open. This proposal specifies the document and the observable conditions an implementation must satisfy.
- The commit hook ran `pnpm check`, the suite behind `pnpm verify`, on Node.js 26.13.1. All 814 tests passed with coverage reporting, and the docs build passed. The initial concurrent run hit test time limits. The lower-concurrency retry passed. `git diff --check` and `pnpm check:pr-title` also passed.

## Merge Danger

**Door** — Two-way. The proposed format has no runtime callers.

**Blast radius** — Documentation.

Record the owner's closure of [adoption issue #26](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/issues/26) after accepting the sandbox evidence. The owner reserved the independent consumer checkout. Independent adoption, controlled live exercises, and private consumer access checks remain unverified.

```release-log
summary: "Record the owner’s closure of adoption issue #26."
impact: "The workflow guide records the sandbox acceptance and the remaining live-validation gaps."
required_action: null
```

## Verification

- Before, the workflow guide called #26 open and deferred. The GitHub issue body and timeline record the owner's November 16 closure.
- After, the guide records the closure and retains the limits of the sandbox evidence.
- The pre-commit hook ran the canonical checks under Node.js 26.13.1. Formatting, lint, type checks, tests, and the documentation build passed.
- PR title validation and `git diff --check` passed.

## Risks and limitations

The change only edits the release workflow guide and can be reverted with a docs-only commit.

pullRequests.body:
## Summary

```text
Ordinary merge → collect the current range → check latest main-push Quality for that exact SHA
  empty, queued or running → wait 15 seconds → recheck current source and baseline → retry
  success → create or refresh the single proposal with immediate prewrite checks
  failure, inconsistent evidence, timeout or stale source → stop
Release merge → verify and tag the exact landing
```

PR #95's release run reached the self-upgrade admission check while Quality for its landing was still running. The manual rerun created #96 after Quality passed. Quality took 4 minutes 38 seconds from creation to success, so this change allows six minutes of polling delays within the existing request count cap. [Initial release run](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44620097797) · [Main-push Quality run](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44620093553)

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: "Wait for the exact main-push Quality result before proposing a release-log self-upgrade."
impact: "An unfinished Quality run within the polling window no longer leaves the pending release proposal stale until a manual rerun."
required_action: null
```

## Evidence

- **Before** the controlled empty-listing fixture failed with “Complete Quality CI evidence is required for the proposed tool revision.”
- **After** the fixture proceeds through missing, queued and in-progress evidence to success. Two later source commits refresh the same PR with the complete range. Timeout, Quality failure, pending evidence at the prewrite check and a superseded source leave state untouched. The exact-landing tag fixture still passes.

## Verification

- The final commit passed the pre-commit hook’s `pnpm check` (the same checks as `pnpm verify`), including the Node test suite and documentation build. A concurrent verification run hit the packaged-CLI fixture’s 90-second timeout.

## Merge danger

**Door** Two-way. The caller activates this code through a reviewed release that updates its immutable workflow and tool pins. Until then, an unfinished Quality run can still require a manual rerun with the existing pin.

**Blast radius** Self-upgrade proposal timing.

pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Refs #76. Request agreement on the Markdown, audience rules, and review binding before implementing the renderer.

```text
validated snapshot + release plan
  → visible breaking warnings, required actions, and source-linked notes
  → review exact Markdown bytes against snapshot ID, version, and contract revision
```

The worked examples cover internal breaking and nonbreaking actions, missing context, and historical commit references. A recapture or changed draft bytes requires a new review. The first review procedure is manual and independent of release proposals.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: Propose the first deterministic release notes contract.
impact: Maintainers can review audience rules and draft freshness before the CLI is implemented.
required_action: null
```

## Evidence

- Before, the development preview selected a section of the technical changelog.
- The RFC shows proposed output from captured evidence, including the warnings, required actions, and source references the offline renderer would produce.
- The pre-commit hook passed its full `pnpm check` suite under Node.js 26.13.1, including all 814 tests and the documentation build.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

**Blast Radius:** Documentation

The renderer and CLI remain follow-up work under #76. Provider integration, proposal storage, publication, and the #77 export schema are outside this PR.
